Safety definitions and counts

Safety describes the known effect, not whether zipmi permits execution. When one recovered firmware row combines behaviors, the displayed class is the highest known impact and the row says so.

Read-Only 126 operations

Reads state and has no known persistent or service effect.

Sensitive 15 operations

Reads or changes credentials, trust, sessions, raw memory, firmware-control state, or other security-sensitive material.

State-Changing 84 operations

Changes configuration or runtime state without a known service interruption or data deletion.

Disruptive 6 operations

Can interrupt a service, session, device, or management connection.

Destructive 13 operations

Can erase data, reset configuration, or replace firmware or persistent state.

Unknown 0 operations

Available evidence does not establish the external effect.

Inventory scope and known gaps

The five provider registration sets and top-level selector census are closed. The 0x30/0x51 selector 0x28 has 22 named child routes with recovered operand and length rules; several D-Bus action names and variable result semantics remain unresolved and are marked Partial. Layouts marked Partial have open byte bounds or unresolved field/behavior meanings. Standard Sensor/SDR/Storage/App/Chassis overrides are inventoried in the compact table and use zipmi's standard command implementations. Group 0x52 commands 0x01/0x02 are system-interface-only and therefore have no supported LAN route.

Live evidence

Authenticated RMCP+ run 20260929T004726Z-90bbc3db-d22b-4660-a34b-e64abb8c8016 reached primary, group, RAS, Intel NM, Sensor, and Storage handlers. The run included an empty 0x32/0x23 request that reached RasSetData; its effect is unknown and the run is not wholly non-mutating evidence. Exact read-only RAS Handshake and Intel Get NM Version requests reached their backends. The guest was then stopped and was not restarted.

48FakeSensorData
30/68 data 3b
Show purpose

Resolves the sensor D-Bus path from the IPMI context and parses a u16le reading from request bytes 2 onward (default 0); byte 1 is ignored. It first writes the u16 reading to com.Supermicro.sdr / com.Supermicro.sensor / fakevalue. Only if that write fails does it set the isfake property on the same service/interface to the boolean from request byte 0. A successful fakevalue write suppresses the isfake write.

62GetLinkStatusCmd
30/68 data 60
Show purpose

Calls the pinned libsmci UtilGetLinkInfo helper. The helper builds LAN_LINK_INFO as IF mode, active interface, four dedicated-link bytes, then three NCSI status bytes; the IPMI handler serializes these in a non-struct order. The dedicated-link bytes include AutoNeg (wire byte 6), a FullDuplex comparison from DuplexMode, Speed mapped as 10→0/100→1/other→2, and a dedicated-interface mode check. It copies dedicated-link byte 3 into byte 0 when byte 3 is 1 and byte 0 is 0.

Read-Only

read-only | Network link-status query.

Show full valueMiddle byte of the helper's 24-bit value: NC-SI Link Status bits 1..4 (speed/duplex); when that nibble is 0xF, the byte instead carries Extended Speed and Duplex bits 31..24. Codes are defined by DMTF DSP0222 Table 51.
1ncsi_link_flagu8
Show full valueHigh byte of the helper's 24-bit value; only bit 0 is populated from NC-SI Link Status bit 0 (0=down, 1=up), upper bits are zero.
2ncsi_auto_negotiate_flagu8
Show full valueLow byte of the helper's 24-bit value; only bit 0 is populated from NC-SI Link Status bit 5 (1=auto-negotiation enabled), upper bits are zero.
3dedicated_link_speed_codeu8LAN_MII_INFO byte 2; value mapping is 10→0, 100→1, other values→2
4dedicated_interface_presentu8LAN_MII_INFO byte 3; dedicated-interface mode check result
5dedicated_link_detectedu8LAN_MII_INFO byte 1; equality result from a D-Bus property comparison
6dedicated_autoneg_valueu8LAN_MII_INFO byte 0; copied from the AutoNeg D-Bus property
7active_interfaceu8LAN_LINK_INFO byte 1; active interface selected by IF-mode helper
8interface_modeu8LAN_LINK_INFO byte 0; result of UtilGetIFMode

70OEMGetSetNVMeSSDParameters
30/68 data 6c
Show purpose

GET uses D-Bus service com.Supermicro.nvme and objects rooted at /com/Supermicro/Nvme/NvmeBp/, reading action/status/info interfaces com.Supermicro.nvmebp.action, .status, .info, and com.Supermicro.nvme.info. GET returns fixed 21-, 16-, or 12-byte property records for subcommands 0, 2, or 0xff; subcommand 1 returns a count byte plus a requested slice of a 215-byte record. The 215-byte backing record is zero-filled before property copies: mapped fields are ClassCode 0..2, VendorId 3..4, SerialNum 5..24, ModelNum 25..64, Port0MaxLinkSpeed 65, Port0MaxLinkWidth 66, Port1MaxLinkSpeed 67, Port1MaxLinkWidth 68, InitialPwrRequirement 69, MaxPowerRequirement 72, CapabilityListPtr 75..76, Manufacturer 77..84, temperature bytes 102..103 and 128, NSS-present flag bit 1 at 125, NSS 126, SmartWarning 127, and PDLU 129; all other bytes are zero. The handler clips page_count with 8-bit subtraction but does not validate page_offset <= 215 before copying; offsets above 215 can trigger an out-of-bounds copy from the BMC process. zipmi's named route rejects those offsets. In the 21-byte subcommand 0 record, byte 1 is constant 1; LocateStatus u32 is split low half at bytes 2..3 and high half at 17..18; Presence u32 is split low half at bytes 4..5 and high half at 19..20; Channel is at offset 0, Id is little-endian u16 at offsets 6..7, Ver u8 at offset 8, and Date is parsed into bytes 9..11. The 16-byte subcommand 2 record contains LocateStatus, Presence, Remove, and RemoveBeforeButton as u32le values split into low/high u16 halves at (0..1, 8..9), (2..3, 10..11), (4..5, 12..13), and (6..7, 14..15), respectively. The 12-byte subcommand 0xff record contains LocateStatus, Presence, and LastPresence as u16le at offsets 0, 2, and 4; bytes 6..11 remain zero from response initialization. SET checks SysLockdownEnable and returns 0xD4 when enabled; otherwise it maps 0=Locate, 1=Dislocate, 2=setButtonEnabled, 3=RedLed, and 4=Remove on the NVMe backplane action interface. Successful SET has no payload; the internal physical effect of Remove is not established by the handler.

State-Changing

mixed; setters change NVMe/backplane LED or state

77OEMGetPSUInfo
30/68 data 79
Show purpose

queries EntityManager PMBusAddr, Bus, and MaxNumber; PMBusAddr is a property-presence gate, not a decoded request address. Body byte 2 must have high nibble 0x7 but its low nibble is ignored. For first trailing byte 0xD0..0xDF, 0xE0..0xED, or 0xF0..0xF6 reads SerialNum, ModelName, or FwVer substrings respectively; otherwise invokes com.smci.psu.info GetPSURaw with body byte 4 followed by body byte 3 (read length), appending returned bytes. Later trailing bytes are not forwarded to GetPSURaw. The matching pinned daemon passes the first argument unchanged as a PMBus command and the second as read length to an ioctl 0x707 transaction on /dev/i2c-%d (one-byte command write, plus requested read when nonzero); it returns the received bytes as a D-Bus byte array. The ioctl helper tries up to four times with 100 ms sleeps between mismatches; the callback retries the helper up to ten times with 100 ms sleeps after failures, then throws std::logic_error('Can't get PSURaw Data after retries.'). The provider's D-Bus/IPMI error-to-completion-code mapping remains unresolved. No write API is called; a PMBus read may still have device-specific read-to-clear effects.

117ClearConfigOption
30/68 data fc
Show purpose

Accepts a u32 option mask. 0x00000004 and 0x02000000 call the anonymous cleanup helper at mapped VA 0x000a84cc (ELF VA 0x000984cc): it enumerates /usr/share/log, byte-prefix matches each entry path against a runtime-initialized global string, stages matching paths, and calls std::filesystem::remove on each. It then removes /usr/share/log/rsyslog_server if present and requests org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager.ReloadUnit("rsyslog.service", "replace"). Mask 0x00000004 additionally emits MEL event 0x7b; 0x02000000 does not. 0x01000000 removes /var/configuration/selstatus, reopens that same path in binary mode, and resizes it to 65536 bytes. Several other recognized masks return success without a visible action; unsupported values return 0xC1.

Destructive

destructive configuration reset; never probe on a production BMC

128OEMCGetSetIPV6Network
30/51 data 09
Show purpose

Top-level operation 0 is a query whose next byte selects 0=DHCPv6/SLAAC mode state (two response bytes), 1=SLAAC status (one byte), 2=current IPv6 address/prefix list (concatenated 17-byte records), 3=DHCPv6 DUID (decoded hex octets), or 4=default IPv6 gateway (16 address bytes plus a zero terminator). Top-level operation 1 writes SLAAC/DHCPv6 mode and IPv6 network settings using PltSetIpv6SlaacStatus, PltGetSetDhcpv6Mode, and UtilSetDHCPPropertyStatus; it requires exactly 20 data bytes after the operation and first reads com.SMCI.Managers.Item.SysLockdown.SysLockdownEnable at xyz.openbmc_project.Settings:/com/SMCI/SysLockdown, returning 0xD4 when true. Operation 2 mutates configured IPv6 addresses/gateway using PltAddIpv6Addr/PltDelIpv6Addr/PltAddIpv6GatewayAddr and requires exactly 16 data bytes. Its first data byte is a mode selector 0..2; the next two bytes are each restricted to 0/1, and mode 2 additionally requires data byte 1 to be zero. Mode 0 maps DHCPv6 mode to 2 and calls PltSetIpv6SlaacStatus(true); mode 1 maps mode to 3 and calls PltSetIpv6SlaacStatus(false); mode 2 retains mode 2 and reaches that helper with its required-zero data byte 1. Data byte 2 selects PltDelIpv6Addr versus the add/reconcile path for mode 2. Operation 2 reads DNSEnabledv6 after setting the normalized DHCPv6 mode; when the property getter returns false and the normalized mode is 2, it calls the setter with false. Unknown operation/query values reject with 0xCC. Remaining setter-field meanings are unresolved; setters remain state-changing and lab-only.

146OEMGetSetMMBIHashKey
30/51 data 20
Show purpose

GET calls getEncHashData on service xyz.openbmc_project.Ipmi.Channel.mmbi_0_bios, object /xyz/openbmc_project/Ipmi/Channel/mmbi_0_bios, interface xyz.openbmc_project.Ipmi.Channel.MMBI. The daemon returns signed-16 status plus ay; zipmi returns the ay only when status is 0 and it is exactly 8 bytes, otherwise completion code 0xD5. SET accepts an opaque byte array of 6–55 bytes, requires its first two bytes nonzero, and forwards it unchanged as D-Bus ay to setEncHashData on the same service/object/interface. The daemon treats byte 0 as the channel selector and bytes 1 onward as candidate Blowfish key material, building a channel-dependent Blowfish schedule from those bytes. It reads the 16-bit BoardId property and expands its little-endian value into four repeated words (8 bytes), encrypts that block, decrypts the ciphertext, and compares the result with a fresh BoardId read. A match stores the encrypted 8-byte block for GET; a mismatch or failed BoardId read clears stored result state. Daemon status 0 produces empty IPMI success and nonzero produces 0xD5. The public checkEncHashData readiness method has no IPMI-provider callsite.

Sensitive
Safety details

mixed/state-changing/sensitive | Requires explicit unsafe authorization; do not probe production hardware.

147OEMGetCMProvision
30/51 data 28
Show purpose

Child-command map includes: 0x00 absent/A=1/A=3 calls ProvisionManager.getROTState/isProvisioning/clearProvisioning; A=4 and child 0x01 call ProvisionManager.doProvisioning, which starts the asynchronous provisioning workflow when accepted. 0x03 returns 3-byte get_rot_cpld_version; 0x09 reads a CPLD register selected by operand A; shipped scripts establish selected uses: register 0x00 bit 4 enables MSMI latching, 0x01 bit 2 is temporarily asserted for surprise reset, 0x08 bits 6/7 are BMC-reset/factory-default flags, 0x0a receives 0x03 for the BoardId-7504 extended fan-delay workaround, and 0x0b is cleared at boot; a separate direct-SPI write of 0x13 to offset 0x18 documents bits 4/0 as BMC-boot-OK/exit-U-Boot, but is not proven to share the D-Bus backend. These examples are not a complete register map. 0x0a returns constant byte 1; 0x0f queries D-Boot status or invokes dumpDboot; 0x20/0x21 perform backup/golden-image update and image erase; 0x30 reads ProvisionManager.getI2CMapProtection, getBmcConsoleLockout, getBmcJtagLockout, getAttestValidation, getROTState, plus SecurityManager.readCPLDFeatbit. Its response has bit2=inverse JTAG lockout, bit3=both CPLD feature bytes != 0xff, bit4=inverse RoT state, bit6=inverse attestation validation; bits 0/1/5 are zero; the I2C and console-lockout results are not packed. 0x54/0x55 are high-impact AC-cycle/CPLD sequences that log MEL, manipulate bits 0x10/0x20 of CPLD register 0x40, sleep/invoke system() commands; 0x84/0x85 return D-Bus bytes, 0x86 calls D-Bus with operand A and returns parsed bytes, 0x87 parses a D-Bus property string; 0xdb conditionally reads a fixed file and returns bounded contents; 0xff returns byte 3. Other child values reject.; child 0x09's matching-daemon low-level reader opens /dev/spitee, issues ioctl 0xc0046b01 with the register index in bits 16..23, and returns the low byte; open/ioctl failure is -5. Direct linkage from the D-Bus callback remains unproven. Child 0xdb reads /usr/share/log/3068db.log only when operand a is 5, returning exactly 256 bytes; longer content is truncated and shorter, missing, or unreadable content is zero-padded. Child 0x0f operand B selects the device path: B=0 /xyz/openbmc_project/cpld_update_mgr/device/Backplane_0_CPLD_0, B=3 /xyz/openbmc_project/cpld_update_mgr/device/AOMboard_1_CPLD_1, B=5 /xyz/openbmc_project/cpld_update_mgr/device/MidplaneSBB_CPLD_1, B=9 /xyz/openbmc_project/cpld_update_mgr/device/Fanboard_1_CPLD_1; the IPMI handler passes per-device index 0. The matching daemon contains a D-Boot dump implementation and writes three 64-KiB blocks to /tmp/cpld_flash_dump.bin (0x30000 bytes on success); it opens with create/truncate flags, so failures can leave an empty or partial file. Provider-side D-Bus exception mapping remains unresolved.

Destructive
Safety details

Destructive subprotocol: includes provisioning reset, image erase/update, CPLD writes, Clear CMOS, and AC-cycle actions; unsafe-gate the outer dispatcher. The pinned child 0x03 daemon may expose three uninitialized stack bytes in its response when the CPLD-device open/ioctl fails.

Host system interface only; no supported LAN route

151OEMAddDelUser
30/51 data 39
Show purpose

Operation 1 creates a user only in an empty slot 1..15 (IPMI user ID 2..16); a populated slot returns 0xCC. It Base64-decodes the credential field, splits username/password at the first ASCII 'G' (0x47), verifies both declared lengths, sets the username and password, then sets the user enabled state to true; success emits MEL event 0x15. Operation 2 requires exactly one slot byte 1..15 (IPMI user ID 2..16); an empty slot returns 0xCC. For a populated slot it resolves that user's name and calls xyz.openbmc_project.Object.Delete.Delete at service xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager, path /xyz/openbmc_project/user/<username>; success emits MEL event 0x16. Both successful operations return no response data.

171GetOOBDataStatus
30/a0 data 09
Show purpose

Accepts only OOB types {1,2,8,12,17,18,19,20,21,22,24}; other type values return 0xC1. Types 1, 2, and 8 stat `/tmp/HII/bios_restore_setting`, `/tmp/HII/bios_restore_dmi`, and `/var/oob/bios_storage`, respectively: the handler requires mode bit 0x100 and reports the file size plus whether it is nonzero. Type 12 has a null path slot and returns zero status/size. Types 17..22 use, respectively, `/tmp/oob/secure_boot_pk`, `/tmp/oob/secure_boot_kek`, `/tmp/oob/secure_boot_db`, `/tmp/oob/secure_boot_dbx`, `/tmp/oob/secure_boot_dbt`, and `/tmp/oob/secure_boot_dbr`; type 24 uses `/tmp/oob/https_boot.der`. For these types, when the `<source>_chksum` sidecar does not already exist, the handler reads the source, sums bytes modulo 256, appends the checksum byte to the source, creates `<source>_chksum` mode 0666, and appends the same byte there. Thus this status command can mutate files.

174UploadOOBData
30/a0 data 0c
Show purpose

Accepts file-type values {0,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,10,12,13,25}. It looks up the selected type in the global 26-entry type-to-output-path map, combines request bytes 2..5 little-endian as a u32 byte count, and formats `mem -f <mapped-path> -r 0xbff00000 -c <count> &> /dev/null`. A null/missing path or zero count returns 0xCC without running the command; system(3) success returns an empty success body and nonzero status returns 0xFF. The map has null paths for types 0, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, and 13, so these accepted values still return 0xCC.

196ReadLockoutGatedRoTCPLDFeatureBits
30/51 data 28 07
Show purpose

Requires operand a=0..3; operand b is forbidden. First calls ProvisionManager.getBmcConsoleLockout with one byte (a+4), then on a nonzero result calls SecurityManager.readCPLDFeatbit with a. A false/failed first call or negative second result maps to 0xd6. The pinned ProvisionManager exposes getBmcConsoleLockout with no arguments, and the pinned SecurityManager exposes readCPLDFeatbit() with no arguments (int64 result); both provider calls have incompatible argument signatures on this image pair. The first mismatch is encountered first, so the second call is not expected to be reached. This is static analysis, not live-tested.

198ReadRoTCPLDRegister
30/51 data 28 09
Show purpose

Requires operand a; accepts any byte value, with no range check, and ignores operand b. Calls smci::core::get_rot_cpld_reg, which invokes SecurityManager.readCpldReg with a; the signed int32 result is returned as its low byte. Matching image scripts identify uses of register 0 bit 4 (MSMI latching), register 1 bit 2 (temporary surprise reset), and register 8 bits 6/7 (BMC reset and factory-default flags); these examples are not a complete register map.

200QueryOrDumpDBoot
30/51 data 28 0f
Show purpose

Requires operand a. A=0 calls provider-local queryDumpDbootStatus and returns its low byte; -1 maps to 0xcc, and optional B is ignored. A=1 requires B as device selector and calls provider-local dumpDboot(B,0), passing per-device index 0; accepted B values map to Backplane_0_CPLD_0 (0), AOMboard_1_CPLD_1 (3), MidplaneSBB_CPLD_1 (5), and Fanboard_1_CPLD_1 (9). Other selectors return -1 and map to 0xd6. The pinned daemon reads the D-Boot JEDEC ID and writes three 64-KiB blocks to /tmp/cpld_flash_dump.bin (0x30000 bytes on success), opening with create/truncate semantics; failed reads/writes can leave a partial file. Provider-side D-Bus exception mapping remains unresolved. The similarly named ProvisionManager methods are not called here.

Show purpose

Ignores optional operands. Emits conditional MEL event 0x11f (Clear CMOS), waits 1 s, reads CPLD register 0x40, then on a valid read raises GPIO 184, writes old|0x10, waits 10 s, restores the exact old register value, and lowers GPIO 184. Invalid register reads still return empty success; system() and write results are ignored.
